import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
cameras = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a bar chart for megapixels distribution
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.histplot(cameras['megapixels'], kde=True, bins=20, label='Megapixels Distribution')
plt.title('Megapixels Distribution Across Camera Models')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')
plt.legend()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a scatter plot for price vs megapixels
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.scatterplot(x='megapixels', y='price_usd', data=cameras, hue='brand')
plt.title('Price vs Megapixels Across Different Brands')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels')
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)')
plt.legend(title='Brand')
plt.savefig('output2.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a bar chart for sensor type distribution
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.countplot(x='sensor_type', data=cameras, order=cameras['sensor_type'].value_counts().index)
plt.title('Sensor Type Distribution Across Camera Models')
plt.xlabel('Sensor Type')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.savefig('output3.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
